headline: Budget, a Democratic Congress and falling oil defined the week
summary: Ottawa's second Carney budget set a $62.3-billion deficit while Democrats locked in control of Congress and still lead two uncalled Senate races. Oil slid toward US$90 on Iran deal hopes, and in Ontario, Toronto froze hiring over a $1.1-billion gap as the province hand-picked eight regional chairs.

top.headline: Carney government's second budget projects $62.3B deficit with $142B in new spending
top.what: Finance Minister Champagne tabled the budget Thursday: a $62.3-billion deficit for 2026-27 and about $142 billion in new spending over five years.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Colom's Mississippi lead nears 3,000 as Hinds County ballots loom
top.what: Democrats are projected to hold at least 259 House seats and a Senate majority; in the two uncalled Senate races, Democratic challengers still lead.
top.why: Democrats take both chambers of Congress in January, reshaping U.S. trade and tariff fights that hit Ontario.

top.headline: Oil steadies near US$92 as markets weigh Iran deal hopes against Hormuz risks
top.what: Brent crude edged up Wednesday after falling to its lowest level since August, as traders balanced hopes for a Qatar-brokered Hormuz deal against continuing attacks on tankers.
top.why: Oil prices drive gas costs and inflation, and the October spike is why the Bank of Canada raised rates.

top.headline: Toronto freezes most hiring as it faces a $1.1-billion budget gap
top.what: With Premier Ford ruling out a second 'New Deal', Toronto has paused most hiring to start closing a projected $1.1-billion shortfall in its 2027 budget.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Markham mayor calls Del Duca's York appointment a conflict of interest
top.what: Ontario named the heads of eight upper-tier councils with 'strong chair' powers, and critics including Markham's mayor say pairing York's chair with Vaughan's mayoralty concentrates power.
top.why: Appointed chairs with veto and staffing powers now steer budgets and planning in York, Peel, Durham and Halton.

top.headline: Canada-U.S. trade talks continue as Democrats vow to repeal tariffs
top.what: Tariffs on Canadian goods remain while talks continue, and the DNC chair says Democrats would move to end them if they win power.
top.why: In the briefing on 5 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Canada loses 4,700 jobs in October; unemployment rises to 6.7%
top.what: Statistics Canada says employment slipped slightly in October and the jobless rate rose 0.2 points to 6.7%, its highest since April.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: House shelves Hegseth impeachment in 211-204 vote
top.what: The Republican-led House voted 211-204 on Tuesday to send Rep. Thomas Massie's impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, effectively ending the effort in this Congress.
top.why: A rare impeachment push against a sitting defence secretary over the Iran war ended for now, but may return in January.
